spec.primaryJobOnMobile: "Is my dinner coming tonight, and do I need to do anything about it?" — a returning subscriber opens the phone to check tonight's status/dish and, occasionally, to skip or pause. Everything else (savings, progress bar, renew nudges) is secondary glanceable context.
spec.currentDesktopLayoutSummary: A 12-column CSS grid (.dash-grid, gap 20px) inside a max-width 1400 centered container with clamp(20-40px) page padding. Above the grid sit stacked full-width blocks in DOM order: order-confirmation banner (post-checkout, dismissable), greeting ribbon (name + lifetime equity line), error toast, OutOfZoneBanner, ProfileBanner, end-of-cycle renew banner, MonthlyWrapStrip. The grid itself renders in three visual rows: row 1 = StatRow (span-12, three tiles in a 3-across sub-grid: Deliveries left / Days left / Saved this cycle); row 2 = HeroToday (span-8, today's dish card, the one TIER_POP dark-navy spotlight) beside QuickActions (span-4, Skip / Plan-a-skip / Pause-Resume buttons); row 3 = PlanProgress (span-12, calendar pill bar + meals-remaining headline + timeline + renew action). Below the grid sits the queued-renewal coda (right-aligned). At <=1024px every grid child already collapses to span-12 (single column) via `.dash-grid > * { grid-column: span 12 }`, and StatRow's internal grid drops to 1-up at <=640px — so today's mobile is a literal vertical stack of full-size desktop cards in DOM order: StatRow(3 stacked tiles) -> HeroToday -> QuickActions -> PlanProgress. That ordering buries tonight's status under three big stat tiles, which is the core problem.
spec.mobileOrganizingPrinciple: Lead with tonight's answer, defer the analytics. HeroToday (today's status + dish) must own the first glance; the three StatRow metrics collapse into one compact horizontal strip (not three viewport-eating cards); QuickActions sits in thumb reach directly under the hero; PlanProgress and all reflective/retention content (savings detail, timeline, renew) move below the fold. Jobs-to-be-Done drives the reorder; Refactoring-UI density drives the metric compression.

elements.name: Greeting ribbon (getGreeting + totalDelivered equity line)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Two stacked text lines at top: 'Good evening, {firstName}.' (14px) plus, when totalDelivered>=5, a muted equity line 'N dinners with us · since {month} · AED X saved vs takeout · N past plans'. marginBottom 20.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep the single greeting line but shrink to ~13px and drop the margin to ~10px. Collapse the equity line to ONE short token (e.g. just 'AED X saved vs takeout' OR 'N dinners with us') instead of the 4-part dot-separated string, which wraps to 2-3 lines at 360px. The full ledger is recall-only context, not the job — push the rest into the savings sheet or omit on mobile.
elements.reorganization: Stays at very top but compressed to one tight line; equity detail truncated to a single most-motivating stat.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI density + JTBD: a personalized hello earns a small slice, but a 4-clause stat string consuming three wrapped lines before the user sees tonight's dinner violates 'lead with the job'.

elements.name: Order-confirmation banner (showOrderBanner, post-checkout)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Dismissable orange-wash card with PartyPopper medallion, 'Your {plan} is active/scheduled', 'First meal arrives {date}. Receipt sent.' + X close. Only after checkout; persists until dismissed.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep full-width and prominent on the one post-checkout visit — it closes the loop on the most expensive action. Tighten padding to ~12px and let the medallion shrink to 32px. It is transient (one session) so its cost is acceptable. Do not merge into the hero.
elements.reorganization: Stays pinned at top above the hero on the post-checkout render only; otherwise absent. Keep the X tappable at 44px.
elements.rationale: Microinteractions (close-the-loop feedback) + Influence (commitment/consistency): confirming the purchase right where the user lands is worth the space, but only transiently.

elements.name: Error toast (actionError)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Red-wash inline strip with message + X, appears on action failure, marginBottom 16.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep as a top inline strip but consider a sticky toast at the bottom safe-area on mobile so it stays in thumb reach and near where the action button was tapped. Ensure the X is 44px. Never hover-only.
elements.reorganization: Either stays top inline or relocates to a bottom-anchored toast above the safe area; immediate visibility of status is non-negotiable.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics visibility of system status + error recovery: a failed skip/pause must be unmissable and dismissable with a real tap target.

elements.name: OutOfZoneBanner
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Non-dismissable gate banner shown when dorm is outside delivery radius; blocks purchase CTAs; links to WhatsApp.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep full-width near the top when active (it is a blocking system condition). Compress copy to one line + WhatsApp tap target at 44px. Rare, so cost is justified when shown.
elements.reorganization: Stays at top, above hero, when present; full-width.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics (error prevention + visibility): a blocking delivery-zone condition must be seen before the user tries to act.

elements.name: ProfileBanner (profileGate missing fields)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Non-dismissable banner listing missing profile fields; blocks plan purchase.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep at top when active but compress to a single tappable row ('Complete your profile to unlock renewals ->'). It gates purchase, not tonight's meal, so it ranks below the hero in priority but stays visible because it is non-dismissable.
elements.reorganization: Stays top, full-width, single compact row with a thumb-sized CTA.
elements.rationale: Norman signifiers + UX-Heuristics: a gate must signify what it blocks and how to clear it, without eating two folds.

elements.name: End-of-cycle renew banner
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Orange-gradient card with '!' medallion, headline that adapts by days-to-end (Last meal tonight / Final day tomorrow / ends in N days) + subline + 'Renew now' pill. Shows only inside the plan-length-scaled window, hidden if queued/scheduled.
elements.densityRecommendation: Compress to a single-line card (medallion 28px, headline + inline 'Renew' chip on one row, drop the subline or make it 11px secondary). On mobile it should sit ABOVE the hero ONLY on the literal last-day (daysToEnd===0) high-urgency case; for the softer multi-day-out variants, demote it to just under the hero so tonight's dinner still leads.
elements.reorganization: Conditional placement: last-day urgency -> above hero; earlier-window -> below hero/QuickActions. Always single-row height.
elements.rationale: JTBD + Influence (scarcity): renewal urgency is real but tonight's status is still the primary job except on the final night when renewal IS the job.

elements.name: MonthlyWrapStrip
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Already a slim 1-line link strip (eyebrow 'wrap' · 'Close out your {cycle}' · days chip · +AED reward · arrow) with a bottom hairline, intentionally subordinate to the hero. Self-renders nothing when ineligible.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~5% when present (one line, may wrap to 2 at 360px)
elements.densityRecommendation: Already mobile-appropriate density. On 360px guard the flex-wrap so it stays one line: drop the middle 'Close out your {cycle}' clause if needed and keep [qualifier wrap] [days chip] [+AED reward ->]. Move it to just below the hero rather than above it on mobile so it doesn't push the hero down.
elements.reorganization: Relocates from above-hero to below-hero (or into the sidebar Now tray per the architecture memory); stays a single quiet line.
elements.rationale: Per project_now_tray_architecture memory it is deliberately subordinate; on mobile that means it must not occupy first-glance space above the hero.

elements.name: StatRow — Tile 1: Deliveries left
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Orange-accent tile, 44px Truck glyph, label 'DELIVERIES LEFT', big 28px/900 number, sub 'of N total'. Part of a 3-across grid, span-12.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Today ~14% each as stacked full tiles (~42% for all three); collapses to 1-up at <=640px which is the worst case
elements.densityRecommendation: Collapse the three tiles into ONE compact horizontal metric strip, 3-across, on mobile (override the <=640px single-column rule for this surface). Each cell: small glyph or none, 11px caps label, ~20-22px number, tiny sub. The whole strip should cost one tile's worth of height (~12-14%), not three. Deliveries-left is the most decision-relevant number so it keeps the orange accent and leftmost position.
elements.reorganization: From a stacked full-height card to the left cell of a single 3-across strip placed directly UNDER the hero (status first, then the numbers that contextualize it).
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI density ('a single metric should rarely consume ~1/3 of a phone viewport') + the product-owner principle to group three metrics as a compact row.

elements.name: StatRow — Tile 2: Days left / Days to start / Plan paused
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: CalendarDays glyph tile; red surface+glyph when active & daysToEnd<=3, neutral otherwise; label switches Days left / Days to start / Plan paused; value is the number or '—' when paused; sub shows ends/starts date or 'resumes where you left off'.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Part of the ~42% stacked-tiles cost today
elements.densityRecommendation: Becomes the middle cell of the compact 3-across strip. Preserve the red urgency state via the number's color/weight AND a small label, never color alone (HIG). When paused, the '—' + 'Plan paused' reads fine in a compact cell. Drop the 44px glyph on mobile to save width.
elements.reorganization: Middle cell of the single metric strip under the hero.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI hierarchy + HIG never-color-alone: urgency can survive compression as long as the label carries it too.

elements.name: StatRow — Tile 3: Saved this cycle (+ benchmark capture CTA, delta pill)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Button-shell tile doubling as benchmark capture. Empty state: dashed border, 'See how much you're saving' + 'Set your benchmark ->'. Populated: PiggyBank glyph, 'SAVED THIS CYCLE', 'AED X' figure, sub copy laddered by state (provenance 'vs AED X/meal · N evenings won back' or 'renew to keep saving'), plus an animated +AED delta pill and a hover-only 'EDIT' hint. At <=1024px it spans both columns on row 2.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Part of the ~42% stacked-tiles cost today; tallest of the three due to sub-copy
elements.densityRecommendation: Split by state. EMPTY (no benchmark): do NOT put the dashed capture CTA in the top strip — move it to a slim full-width row just below the metric strip, or into the savings bottom sheet; it is a setup task, not a glanceable metric. POPULATED: show only 'AED X saved' as the third cell of the compact strip (number + tiny 'vs AED X/meal'); move the evenings/renew sub-copy + the EDIT affordance into a tap-to-open bottom sheet (the hover-only EDIT hint is invisible on touch and must become an explicit tap). Keep the delta-pill celebration but anchor it so it doesn't overflow the narrow cell.
elements.reorganization: Populated -> third cell of the strip; rich detail + edit -> bottom sheet on tap. Empty -> its own slim setup row below the strip.
elements.rationale: Microinteractions (progressive disclosure into a sheet) + UX-Heuristics (no hover-only affordance on touch) + JTBD (savings is reflective, not the open-the-app job).

elements.name: HeroToday — active state (tonight's dish card)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: span-8 TIER_POP dark-navy gradient card (the one spotlight on the page): 'TONIGHT'S DISH' eyebrow, large animated dish name (clamp 28-40px), description, MealTag + HeatBar row, footer with status badge + countdown caption ('Arriving in ~Nh') + 'View dish ->'. Day-1 gold pulse badge floats top-right on first day.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Today pushed below ~42% of stat tiles; the card itself is ~35-40% of viewport
elements.densityRecommendation: Promote to the very first card after the top banners — this is the answer to the primary job and must own first-glance. Keep it the bold dark spotlight (it earns full width/space). Tighten internal padding from clamp(26-36) toward ~20px on mobile, cap dish name around 28-30px so a long name doesn't wrap to 3 lines, keep the status badge + countdown footer fully visible without scroll. Keep the Day-1 badge.
elements.reorganization: Moves ABOVE StatRow and QuickActions to be the first content block; full-width; slightly denser padding.
elements.rationale: JTBD (the one job) + Refactoring-UI (the single TIER_POP earns its space) + Norman (close the gulf of evaluation — 'is dinner coming?' answered instantly).

elements.name: HeroToday — inactive states (Scheduled / Skipped / Paused / Delivered / Off / Resumed-after-cutoff)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Same card on TIER1 + orange edge-wash with a state headline (e.g. 'You skipped today.', 'Your plan is paused.', "You're all set.") + subtitle + same footer badge/caption/link. Animated transitions between states.
elements.densityRecommendation: Same first-glance promotion and padding tightening as the active state. These states ARE the status answer in their own right, so they stay full-width and lead. Ensure the footer caption ('Resume available tomorrow', 'Credit safe — back tomorrow') is visible without scroll.
elements.reorganization: Same slot as active hero — first content card; the state machine just swaps interior copy.
elements.rationale: JTBD + visibility of status: whatever today's state is, it is the first thing the user needs to see.

elements.name: QuickActions — Skip / Plan-a-skip / Pause-Resume buttons + skip-quota chip
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: span-4 TIER1 card beside the hero. 'QUICK ACTIONS' eyebrow + up to three full-width pill buttons (Skip tonight's meal with quota chip; Plan a skip; Pause/Resume which morphs through pending/success/planned-pause/consumed-credit states). 14px vertical padding gives ~48px tap height.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~30-38% of viewport for the full card with 2-3 buttons
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep the buttons full-width (they are already ~48px tall — good for touch) and place the card DIRECTLY under the hero so the primary action sits in thumb reach. Drop the 'QUICK ACTIONS' eyebrow + card chrome/padding on mobile — let the buttons read as a bare action stack under the hero. Demote 'Plan a skip' (future-dated, secondary) into a 'More options' bottom sheet so first-glance shows only the two relevant primary actions (Skip tonight + Pause/Resume).
elements.reorganization: From a side card (span-4) to a chromeless full-width button stack immediately below the hero; secondary 'Plan a skip' moves into a sheet.
elements.rationale: iOS HIG (primary actions in thumb reach, 44px+ targets) + Microinteractions (progressive disclosure of the future-dated secondary action) + Refactoring-UI (shed card chrome that does not earn its height on mobile).

elements.name: Skip-quota chip (inside Skip button) + lock states (cutoff/no-delivery/exhausted)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Right-aligned uppercase chip on the Skip button ('N left' / 'Last one' / 'None left' / 'Past 2 PM' / 'No delivery' / 'Trial only'); button disables + outlines when locked, tooltip carries the reason.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Inside the Skip button — no extra height
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep the chip inline on the button. CRITICAL: the disabled-reason currently lives in a hover Tooltip which does not exist on touch — surface the reason as visible inline text below the button (or in the sheet) so the user understands why Skip is locked without hovering.
elements.reorganization: Chip stays on the button; the lock reason becomes visible inline text instead of hover-only.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics (no hover-only info on touch; help users recognize, not guess) + the skip-irreversible constraint makes clear state communication essential.

elements.name: PlanProgress — meals-remaining headline + calendar pill bar
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: span-12 TIER2 card: plan identity eyebrow, '36 of N meals remaining' big number, a date-pegged calendar pill bar (one pill per working day, orange=delivered, hatched=skipped, plain=upcoming, today ring), hover tooltips, clickable future pills to skip/un-skip.
elements.densityRecommendation: Move below the fold (after hero + actions + metric strip). Keep the meals-remaining headline and the pill bar — the bar is glanceable progress and survives mobile width well since pills are flex:1. BUT pill hover tooltips and click-to-skip are pointer affordances: on touch, a pill tap should open a small bottom sheet showing that day's date/state and a Skip/Un-skip button (replacing hover tooltip + click). Widen pill min-width slightly and rely on the sheet rather than the 3px pill as the tap target.
elements.reorganization: Relocates to below-fold; pill interaction shifts from hover-tooltip/click to tap-opens-sheet.
elements.rationale: Microinteractions + iOS HIG (tap targets, bottom sheets) + Norman (the bar's conceptual model of 'you are here' is good; just re-map the interaction to touch).

elements.name: PlanProgress — planned-pause banner + boundary marker
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Inline navy-wash callout above the bar ('Pause planned for {date}' + underlined Cancel link) plus a 1px navy marker line in the bar at the pause-start pill.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep as a compact full-width row above the bar when present. The Cancel link must become a real >=44px tap target (currently a small underlined text button). Keep the structural marker in the bar.
elements.reorganization: Stays attached to the top of the PlanProgress block (below fold); Cancel grows to a tappable control.
elements.rationale: iOS HIG tap targets + Norman mapping (the banner+marker pairing keeps cause and location visible).

elements.name: PlanProgress — stats line (delivered / skipped / untraced) + timeline (Started -> Ending, Days left) + renew action
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Count-only stats line; a Started -> Ending timeline row with a right-aligned 'Days left' big number (or paused extension note); and a contextual action block (Plan-ended renew card, Renew -> chip in last-7-days, or a begins/resume note).
elements.densityRecommendation: This duplicates numbers already in the top metric strip (Days left) and the headline (meals remaining). On mobile, trim: keep the Started->Ending dates and the renew action, drop the redundant 'Days left' big number (it's in the strip) and let the delivered/skipped line shrink to 11px. Let the timeline row wrap gracefully. The Renew action here can be the single renew entry point when the top renew banner is suppressed.
elements.reorganization: Stays at bottom of PlanProgress (deep below fold); de-duplicated against the top metric strip; timeline allowed to wrap to two rows.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI (remove redundant chrome; don't show the same number twice) + JTBD (timeline/renew is planning context, lowest urgency).

elements.name: Queued-renewal coda ('Up next' chip + plan + start date + Manage)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Right-aligned chromeless inline row below the grid: hairline marker, outlined gold 'Up next' chip, plan name + 'Starts {date}' (+ 'Tentative' pill when paused), and a quiet gray 'Manage' hover-link.
elements.densityRecommendation: Switch from right-aligned to left-aligned full-width on mobile and let it wrap to two lines if needed (the single-line ellipsis on a 360px width would clip the plan/date). The 'Manage' link must be a real >=44px tap target, not a hover-styled gray link. Keep the 'Up next' chip as the visual anchor.
elements.reorganization: From right-aligned single line to left-aligned wrapping row at the very bottom; Manage becomes a proper tap target.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics (no hover-only/clip on touch) + iOS HIG tap targets; it is low-priority committed-state info so it stays last.

elements.name: Skip confirmation modal (irreversible)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Centered 440px modal over blurred backdrop: 'Skip tonight's meal?' H2, plain-English reassurance, a 2-col data row (End date +1 day / Skips left N/total), an uppercase red 'This can't be undone after confirm' note, Cancel + 'Skip tonight' buttons.
elements.densityRecommendation: Convert from a centered dialog to a bottom sheet anchored to the safe area so the confirm/cancel buttons sit in thumb reach. Keep the irreversibility note prominent (the skip-is-irreversible constraint forbids any undo). Buttons full-width stacked or side-by-side at >=48px. No undo affordance after confirm.
elements.reorganization: Centered modal -> bottom sheet; actions in thumb zone; same three-tier hierarchy.
elements.rationale: iOS HIG (sheets, thumb-reach actions) + the locked skip-irreversible constraint (confirmation must be clear and final).

elements.name: Pause confirm / Queued-pause warning / Cancel-planned-pause modals
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Centered modals: Pause confirm (uses your 1 free pause, end date extends, 'Pause from a future date instead ->' link); Queued-pause warning (PauseCircle medallion, two-column This-plan/Next-plan impact summary, acknowledge); Cancel-planned-pause (returns the free pause).
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Full overlay; the queued-pause warning is the tallest (medallion + 2-col grid + note)
elements.densityRecommendation: Convert all three to bottom sheets with thumb-reach actions. For the queued-pause warning, stack the two impact cards vertically (the 2-col grid is cramped at 360px) and keep the 'Pause from a future date instead' link as a >=44px row. Allow internal scroll if content exceeds sheet height.
elements.reorganization: Centered modals -> bottom sheets; multi-column impact grids stack to single column.
elements.rationale: iOS HIG (bottom sheets, stacked content on narrow widths) + Norman (make the consequence of pausing legible before commit).

elements.name: FutureSkipModal / PlanPauseModal / SavingsBenchmarkModal (date/slider pickers)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Separate modal components opened from QuickActions 'Plan a skip', the pause 'future date' link, and the StatRow savings tile respectively (date pickers / AED slider with live preview).
elements.densityRecommendation: Render as bottom sheets on mobile with native-feeling date/slider controls and a thumb-reach confirm button. The savings benchmark sheet is also where the populated-savings detail + EDIT lives (re-homed from the StatRow tile). These were not fully read here — confirm their internal layouts honor 44px controls and safe areas.
elements.reorganization: Picker modals -> bottom sheets; savings sheet absorbs the savings-detail/edit that moved off the metric strip.
elements.rationale: Microinteractions (progressive disclosure) + iOS HIG (sheet + native pickers).

elements.name: Resume welcome overlay + checkout success overlay (full-screen celebration)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Full-screen pointer-events:none overlays: 3-phase resume (checking ring -> Truck/Moon medallion + 'Welcome back') and a 3s checkout success (checkmark medallion + confetti + 'You're in'). Honor prefers-reduced-motion.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep essentially as-is — they are transient full-screen moments that work on mobile. Verify medallion/text sizing (clamp already used) fits 360px and that safe-area insets don't clip the centered stack. pointer-events:none means the dashboard stays interactive underneath, which is correct.
elements.reorganization: No structural change; just verify sizing/safe-area on small viewports.
elements.rationale: Microinteractions + emotional design (Norman's visceral level): the celebratory feedback is worth keeping intact on mobile.

proposedMobileScanOrder: Order-confirmation banner (post-checkout only) / OutOfZoneBanner / ProfileBanner (gates, when active)
End-of-cycle renew banner (above hero ONLY on last-day urgency)
QuickActions (Skip + Pause/Resume as a bare button stack in thumb reach)
Compact 3-across metric strip (Deliveries left · Days left · Saved)
MonthlyWrapStrip (slim) / softer renew banner if not last-day
spec.crossCuttingNotes: Reusable patterns that recur across dashboard surfaces: (1) Compact 3-across metric strip — the same StatRow compression applies anywhere three KPIs are stacked (e.g. /plan, /history). Build it as a shared MobileMetricStrip. (2) Modal -> bottom sheet conversion — every confirm/picker on this surface (skip, pause, queued-pause, cancel-pause, future-skip, plan-pause, savings benchmark) should route through one shared BottomSheet primitive with thumb-reach actions and safe-area padding; this will be reused on every route that has modals. (3) Hover-only info is the single biggest touch hazard here — QuickActions Tooltip lock reasons, PlanProgress pill tooltips, the StatRow 'EDIT' hint, and the 'Manage'/'Cancel' hover-links all need explicit touch equivalents (visible inline text or tap-to-sheet). Establish a rule: no information or affordance may live solely in :hover on mobile. (4) Banners stack (order/out-of-zone/profile/renew/wrap) should share a single compact mobile banner component with one-line layout and 44px tap targets. (5) The light theme + brand-orange #f57f20 ceiling and the deliberately-imprecise countdown all carry over unchanged.
openDecisions: StatRow on mobile currently collapses to 1-up at <=640px (stat-row internal media query). The recommendation is the opposite — a compact 3-across strip. Confirm we override the existing <=640px single-column rule for this dashboard-home strip (the 3-across compaction is the whole point of the metric-density principle).

Where should the metric strip sit relative to the hero — immediately under the hero (status-then-numbers, recommended) OR under QuickActions? This affects whether the user sees actions or numbers second.

End-of-cycle renew banner placement is conditional in the proposal (above hero only on daysToEnd===0). Confirm the product owner wants tonight's hero to outrank renewal on every day except the final night, or whether renewal should always lead inside its window.

Savings tile EMPTY state (benchmark not set): keep it as a visible slim setup row below the strip, OR hide it entirely on mobile and surface benchmark capture only from the savings sheet / a one-time prompt? It's a setup task competing for first/second-fold space.

'Plan a skip' (future-dated) is proposed to move into a 'More options' sheet so first-glance shows only Skip-tonight + Pause/Resume. Confirm demoting it off the primary stack is acceptable, or whether it must stay a visible third button.
Per the Now-tray architecture memory, the MonthlyWrapStrip may belong in the sidebar Now tray rather than inline on mobile. Decide whether mobile keeps the inline strip, relies on the tray, or both.

PlanProgress pill bar interaction on touch: confirm a pill tap should open a per-day bottom sheet (date + Skip/Un-skip) since hover tooltips and 3px click targets don't work on phones — this is a behavior change, not just layout.

The FutureSkipModal, PlanPauseModal, and SavingsBenchmarkModal internals were not read in this pass; their mobile sheet layouts (date pickers, AED slider, live preview) need a separate review to confirm 44px controls and safe-area handling.

spec.surface: Plan & Checkout (/dashboard/plan and /dashboard/explore-plans — same PlanClient.tsx, mode-switched)
spec.primaryJobOnMobile: Two jobs split by mode. On /dashboard/plan: "Where does my current plan stand right now, and what's next?" (read status, manage start date / planned pause, glance at setup). On /dashboard/explore-plans: "Pick a plan and pay" — choose a tier, set the start date, get to Stripe. The redesign must optimize each mode for its own single job rather than averaging them.
spec.currentDesktopLayoutSummary: Single centered column (max-width 1280) on a cream page gradient. /plan mode stacks: cancel banner → H1 header → dark ActivePlanCallout (TIER_POP) with hero days-left + auto-fit metric grid → optional QueuedSubCallout (TIER2, orange left-rail) → "switch plans?" TIER2 strip → PlanSetupCard (TIER2, two auto-fit dial zones) → a 2-column reference row (Pricing FAQ left, Past plans right, stacks under 1024px) → footer. /explore mode replaces the middle with: optional paused notice → 3-column trust strip → preference/week pills row + Religious VegDayPicker → OutOfZoneBanner → plans-grid (1/2/4 cols at 640/1024) → CheckoutPanel that slide-ins on selection and is position:sticky bottom only ≥1024px. CheckoutPanel internally is a receipt header (identity left, big orange total right) + gradient hairline + optional credit row + optional veg-day picker + a 2-col action strip (DateField | CTA) that collapses to 1col under 640px, plus a 2-col helper row.
spec.mobileOrganizingPrinciple: One job per screen, top-to-bottom, with the single most-decision-relevant number leading. On /plan that is the status hero (days left / starts-in); on /explore it is the price-per-plan leading into a thumb-reachable checkout. Compress every supporting metric/dial into tight multi-up rows so the lead number and the next action are both reachable in the first glance, and push all "manage / why / history" detail into accordions or bottom sheets rather than long inline stacks.

elements.name: cancelBanner (checkout_canceled status strip)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Full-width neutral TIER strip at top, text left + × dismiss right, marginBottom 22.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep full-bleed but tighten to a single 13px line with the × as a 44px tap target. It is transient and reassuring (no charge made); do not let it wrap to 3 lines and shove the header below the fold. Auto-dismiss timer optional.
elements.reorganization: Same position (very top, above header) but constrained height; × becomes a proper 44px hit area instead of an 18px glyph.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics (visibility of status) — it answers 'did my money get taken?'. iOS HIG 44pt for the dismiss. It earns first-glance only because it is rare and anxiety-reducing.

elements.name: header (H1 'My plan.' / 'Explore plans.' + supporting paragraph)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: clamp(34-48px) 700-weight H1 with orange period, 15px muted paragraph (max 640), marginBottom 48.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~22% of viewport at the clamp floor of 34px plus 48px bottom margin and a 2-line paragraph
elements.densityRecommendation: Cut the 48px bottom margin to ~16-20px. Drop H1 to ~28px on mobile. On /plan, demote or drop the supporting paragraph ('current subscription, account details, past plans all in one place') — it is orientation copy a returning user doesn't need every visit; keep on /explore where the first-timer needs framing but trim to one line.
elements.reorganization: Stays top but shrinks dramatically so the status hero (/plan) or the trust strip+grid (/explore) climbs into first glance instead of being pushed down by a 90px title block.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI (constrained spacing; hierarchy from scale not whitespace) + Jobs-to-be-Done (the title is not the job; the status/price is). Desktop's 48px breathing margin is exactly the 'fluid breathing' the brief says to break from.

elements.name: ActivePlanCallout (TIER_POP dark card: plan name, date range, status dot, hero days-left, metric grid)

proposedMobileScanOrder: plans-grid (recommended Monthly Premium first, then alternatives)
spec.crossCuttingNotes: Reusable mobile components this surface needs that almost certainly recur elsewhere in the dashboard: (1) A BottomSheet primitive — both modals (ChangeStartDate, Cancel-planned-pause), the CheckoutPanel, and the DateField calendar should all become sheets; build one and reuse. (2) A MobileDatePicker sheet wrapping DateField — the calendar appears in CheckoutPanel AND both change-start modals, so the touch fixes (44pt cells, inline 'why disabled' instead of hover/title tooltips, no clip) land once. (3) A 'CompactMetricRow' (3-across label/value band) used by ActivePlanCallout's metric grid and reusable by any dashboard card with auto-fit minmax stat tiles that sprawl on mobile. (4) A FullWidthActionButton with explicit disabled-reason caption — every disabled CTA here (Renew out-of-zone, Change start used, Explore-when-paused, Checkout out-of-zone) currently leans on a hover/title Tooltip that does nothing on touch; the pattern of 'disabled + visible reason line' is the cross-cutting fix. (5) StatusDot + Eyebrow + PlanGlyph are shared tokens already — verify they read at mobile sizes. The hover-only Tooltip component is the single biggest cross-cutting touch hazard on this surface and recurs wherever Tooltip is used.
openDecisions: The two modes (/plan vs /explore) are one file but want opposite hierarchies on mobile — should the redesign treat them as two genuinely separate mobile layouts (status-first vs buy-first) rather than one shared scroll? The proposed scan order above leads with the /explore buy-flow; /plan's management cards would lead instead. Confirm we optimize each route independently.

Should the CheckoutPanel become a bottom sheet that rises on plan selection (thumb-reachable, classic mobile commerce pattern) instead of an inline slide-in the user must scroll down to find? Desktop sticky is already disabled <1024px, so mobile currently leaves the CTA buried mid-scroll.

On mobile /explore, do we float the recommended Monthly Premium card to the TOP of the single-column grid (lead with the recommendation) or preserve the desktop tier order Trial → Weekly Flex → Premium → Max?
PlanCard feature lists: collapse to 2-3 lines + 'details' disclosure per card, or keep full lists and accept tall cards? This trades scannability against full information at a glance.

The hover/title Tooltips on disabled CTAs and the 'Tentative'/non-delivery-day explanations are invisible on touch — confirm we replace ALL of them with always-visible inline captions (and whether that changes desktop too, or mobile-only).

ActivePlanCallout dark TIER_POP card: is the dark treatment intentional like the marketing/onboarding surfaces, or should it follow the light dashboard intent on mobile? (It already lives in the light dashboard, so likely stays — confirm it isn't an accidental dark-on-light island when compressed.)
PlanSetupCard on mobile: compress to a 2-up dial grid always-visible, or collapse behind a 'Your setup' expander since it's pure reference and not the job?

spec.primaryJobOnMobile: "What am I getting tonight, and when does it arrive?" The customer opens this on a phone to confirm today's dish + delivery ETA, then optionally scan the rest of this week and peek at next week. Everything else (preference change, dish macros, renew prompts) is secondary to that one tonight-focused answer.
spec.currentDesktopLayoutSummary: Single centered column (max-width 1400) with a page header ("My menu." + preference row), then three vertically-stacked sections each with an Eyebrow + hairline divider: (1) Today spotlight as a full-width 7fr/5fr two-column hero (text left, framed photo right, min-height 320); (2) This week as a 3-across grid of 6 full WeekDayCards (TIER2, today bumped to TIER1 with orange pulsing ring); (3) Next week as a denser 6-across strip of compact "preview" WeekDayCards (TIER3, orange top-wash). A dish-detail modal (centered, max 560) opens on card tap. Existing media queries already stack the hero at 768 and step the grids down (this-week 3→2→1 at 640/420; next-week 6→4→3→2 at 1024/640/420).
spec.mobileOrganizingPrinciple: Tonight first, this week second, next week as a peek — collapse the breathing desktop rhythm into a tight vertical timeline. The Today spotlight is the only element that earns big vertical space (it answers the primary job); everything below it compresses into scannable list/grid rows so the user can reach "this week" without a long scroll, and "next week" stays a deliberately small, low-commitment strip at the bottom.

elements.reorganization: Stays at top, smaller. Compress the gap between it and the preference row so header + preference read as one compact unit, not two breathing rows.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI hierarchy + constrained spacing: the title earns identity but not size on a phone; reclaim its vertical cost for the spotlight below.

Ensure the "Change" tap target is padded to 44px height even though it renders as small text — it is the only navigational action in the header.
elements.reorganization: Keep directly under the title. Let it wrap to at most two lines; do not let the four-part dot-separated string wrap into a ragged 3-line block as it will at 360px.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics 44px target + recognition: preference and delivery window are reference info, not the job; keep visible but demoted. The Change link is a real action so it must be thumb-tappable.

elements.name: Section Eyebrows + hairline dividers ("Today's delivery" / "This week" / "Next week")
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Each section opens with an Eyebrow chip + a flex:1 hairline rule, marginBottom 14, section marginBottom 32.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep all three as wayfinding labels but cut the inter-section marginBottom from 32 to ~20 and the eyebrow marginBottom from 14 to ~10. The hairline rule can stay (cheap, aids scan segmentation). Note the first eyebrow flips to "Tonight" when resumedAfterCutoff — preserve that.
elements.reorganization: Sticky-section labels are optional; simplest is to keep them inline but tighter. They become the scan anchors of the vertical timeline.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI density: three sections need separators to avoid a wall of cards, but desktop's generous 32px gaps waste phone height. Tighten without removing the structural cue.

elements.name: TodaySpotlight — active state (dish name, description, macro strip, countdown, dorm chip, photo)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: TIER_POP navy card, 7fr/5fr grid, min-height 320. Left: Eyebrow "Tonight's dish", 24-36px dish heading, description (max 54ch), 2-3 cell macro strip (Calories/Protein/Spice), live countdown pill (Truck icon, orange when urgent) with dorm pill. Right: framed 16:10-ish photo. Already stacks to one column at 768 with photo moving below text.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~70-90% of viewport when stacked (photo + text + macros + countdown)
elements.densityRecommendation: This is the one element that earns space — but re-order INSIDE it for mobile. Lead with the photo (compact 16:10), then dish name, then the live countdown pill promoted directly under the name (it is the time-sensitive answer), then the macro strip as the compact 3-across row it already is, then the description LAST (or truncated to ~2 lines with the full text living in the dish modal on tap). Goal: dish name + ETA visible without scrolling; macros and description can sit just below the fold.
elements.reorganization: Stacked single column (existing 768 query already does this). Reorder children so countdown rises above the description; consider shrinking photo to ~180-200px tall so name+ETA clear the ~700px first-glance budget. Keep the navy TIER_POP treatment — it is the page's intentional focal contrast, not a theme violation.
elements.rationale: Jobs-to-be-Done: tonight's dish + ETA IS the job. Refactoring-UI: it earns the largest block, but description prose is the lowest-value pixels there, so it yields to the countdown. Microinteractions: the 30s-refreshing countdown is the live status signal and belongs high.

elements.name: TodaySpotlight — Sunday / rest-day empty state
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: TIER1 cream card (#faf2dd), 56px vertical padding, centered Moon icon + "Sunday — no delivery" + "Rest up. Next delivery Monday at 7 PM."
elements.densityRecommendation: Cut the 56px padding to ~32px on mobile. The centered Moon + two lines is fine but should not occupy a third of the screen for an empty state — compress so "This week" rises closer to the fold on Sundays.
elements.reorganization: Same position (top), shorter. It still anchors the slot but with far less air.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI: an empty state has the least information to surface, so it should claim the least height — the inverse of how desktop currently pads it.

elements.name: TodaySpotlight — resumed-after-cutoff state
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: TIER1 card with orange edge-wash, Moon icon, "No delivery tonight.", paragraph naming next delivery (7–8 PM), faint reassurance line about the moved meal slot.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep all copy (it closes the Gulf of Evaluation — explains why nothing arrives) but tighten the clamp paddings and the gap from 16 to ~12. The two paragraphs can stay; they are load-bearing reassurance, not filler.
elements.reorganization: Same top slot. The orange wash + Moon stay as the brand-consistent 'no delivery but all is well' signal.
elements.rationale: Norman conceptual model: this state must explain itself so the user doesn't think delivery is broken — so it keeps its copy even on mobile, just at tighter spacing.

elements.name: This-week WeekDayCard grid (6 full cards, Mon–Sat)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: 3-across TIER2 grid, gap 16. Each card: header (day · state chip · date), 16:10 photo, dish name (clamp 2), MealTag + HeatBar footer, veg/non-veg spine. Today card bumps to TIER1 with 2px orange border + breathing pulse + Sparkles "Today" chip. Media queries step to 2-col at 640, 1-col at 420.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: At 1-col (≤420) each full card is ~tall (photo+header+body); 6 of them = multiple screens of scroll
elements.densityRecommendation: Force 2-across on the primary 390px viewport (not the current 1-col-at-420). Six full-photo single-column cards is an excessive scroll for what is mostly a glanceable week strip. 2-across keeps photos legible while halving vertical run. Today's card can optionally span full width / 2 columns as the visual standout since it carries the orange pulse and is the most important cell. Keep the day/date/state chip header — it is the recognition-over-recall scaffold.
elements.reorganization: 3-col desktop → 2-col mobile (override the current ≤420 1-col rule; reserve 1-col only as a last resort below ~340px). Promote today's cell to a wider/taller treatment so the pulsing focal card isn't shrunk into a tiny 2-up cell.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI density + Jobs-to-be-Done: the week is a scan, not a read; 2-across respects phone height. The today-pulse + Sparkles chip is the in-grid 'you are here' status signal (visibility of system status) and deserves extra size.

elements.name: WeekDayCard — no-delivery states (skipped / paused / pause-start / in-pause)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Dim card, Moon-family chip with reason label ("Not tonight"/"Skipped"/"Paused"/"Pause begins"), muted color, no orange focal treatment.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Same as a normal card cell
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep the chip-label system intact — it is never color-alone (Moon/Lock icon + text), which satisfies the touch/accessibility constraint. At 2-across these still read fine. Do not collapse them into a different size than their siblings; the grid uniformity is what makes the dimmed ones legible by contrast.
elements.reorganization: Inline in the same this-week grid, same cell size as active cards. The dimming + icon do the differentiation work, not size.
elements.rationale: Norman signifiers + UX-Heuristics: the reason chip closes the Gulf of Evaluation (why no meal that day) and must survive on mobile; never reduce to color-only on touch.

elements.name: WeekDayCard — plan-ends state (grayscale photo, lock overlay, "Renew to unlock" chip, dashed border, routes to /explore-plans)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Grayed gray-tan surface, dashed border, opacity 0.78, grayscale+dimmed photo, centered lock badge overlay, Lock chip "Renew to unlock"; tapping routes to explore-plans instead of opening the modal.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Same as a normal card cell
elements.densityRecommendation: Preserve all four signals (grayscale, dashed border, lock overlay, chip) — they are mutually reinforcing and the only on-page renew prompt. Ensure the whole card stays a 44px+ tap target since it is effectively a CTA to /explore-plans. Could optionally surface a single explicit "Renew" pill at the end of the week grid on mobile so the action isn't only discoverable by tapping a grayed card.
elements.reorganization: Lives in whichever week grid the expired days fall in (this-week or next-week). The card IS the CTA; keep the tap-routes-to-renew behavior.
elements.rationale: Microinteractions discoverable trigger + Norman mapping: the card's look promises 'renew' and the tap pays it off. On a phone a grayed card can read as merely disabled, so consider an explicit renew affordance as a fork (see open decisions).

elements.name: Next-week WeekDayCard preview strip (6 compact cards)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: 6-across TIER3 grid, gap 10, compact 4:3 cards with orange top-wash, no veg spine. Media queries step 6→4 at 1024, →3 at 640, →2 at 420.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: At ≤420 it's 2-across compact cards = a few rows of scroll at the very bottom
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep it as the densest, lowest strip — this is correct. On the 390px primary it should be 2-across (small Android 360 also 2). It is a 'peek ahead', so smaller-than-this-week is the right hierarchy. Consider 3-across at 390 to keep it visibly denser than the 2-across this-week grid and reinforce 'preview, not primary'.
elements.reorganization: Stays at the bottom, denser than this-week. The whole strip could even be lazy/below-fold without harm. Optionally make next-week a horizontally-scrolling row instead of a wrapped grid to keep it to one screen-height and signal 'secondary, swipe to browse'.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI tiered surfaces + Jobs-to-be-Done: next week is the lowest-priority job; its density and position must keep it visibly subordinate to this-week. A horizontal scroll is a strong 'this is a peek' signifier (open decision).

elements.name: DishDetailModal (photo, day·date eyebrow, name, description, Calories/Protein grid, MealTag + spice, Close button)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Centered fixed overlay, blurred backdrop, max-width 560, padding 32, 16:10 photo, 28px name, 2-col macro grid, full-width Close button. Opens on card tap; Escape closes.
elements.densityRecommendation: Convert from a centered dialog to a bottom sheet on mobile: slide up from the bottom, rounded top corners, respect the safe-area inset, and put the Close affordance (and a grab handle) within thumb reach at the bottom — the full-width Close button already exists, keep it pinned. Add tap-on-backdrop-to-dismiss (already present) plus swipe-down-to-dismiss. This is the right home for the full dish description that we truncated in the spotlight.
elements.reorganization: Centered modal (desktop) → bottom sheet (mobile). Content order is already good (photo → name → description → macros → tag); keep it. The 2-col macro grid stays 2-col, it's already compact.
elements.rationale: iOS HIG + Microinteractions progressive disclosure: dense per-dish detail belongs in a bottom sheet reachable by thumb, not a center-screen dialog. This lets the spotlight and cards stay lean while detail lives one tap deep.

proposedMobileScanOrder: TodaySpotlight (photo → dish name → countdown → macros → description-truncated)
Next-week preview strip (2-3 across or horizontal scroll, densest)
spec.crossCuttingNotes: WeekDayCard is shared by this-week (full) and next-week (preview) and already encodes variant/state/no-delivery logic — its mobile tuning (2-across full, denser preview, 44px tap targets, never-color-alone chips) is a reusable pattern any other card-grid surface should copy. The Eyebrow + hairline-divider section header is a shared _shared/ component; the tightened mobile spacing (eyebrow mb ~10, section mb ~20) should be applied wherever Eyebrow sections appear, not just here. The DishDetailModal → bottom-sheet conversion is a pattern that should apply to every dashboard modal on mobile (per the iOS HIG lens) — establish it once and reuse. The live computeCountdown pill (Truck icon, orange-when-urgent, 30s refresh, deliberately imprecise ~Nh) is a status microinteraction shared in spirit with the dashboard HeroToday — keep both consistent. The TIER_POP navy spotlight against the light interface is intentional contrast, not a theme to unify.
openDecisions: This-week grid on the 390px primary: 2-across (my recommendation, overriding the current ≤420 1-column rule) vs keeping the existing 1-column stack. 1-col gives bigger photos but turns the week into a long scroll.
Should today's this-week card span full width / 2 columns to stay the visual focal point, or remain a single cell equal to its siblings (relying only on the orange pulse to stand out)?

Next-week strip: wrapped 2-3 across grid (current approach, scrolls vertically) vs a single-row horizontal scroller (stronger 'peek, secondary' signifier, keeps it to one screen height). Horizontal scroll hides items off-edge — acceptable for a low-priority preview?

In the TodaySpotlight, truncate the dish description to ~2 lines with full text in the bottom sheet, vs keep the full description inline. Trade-off: getting the countdown above the fold vs showing the full dish prose immediately.

plan-ends cards are the only on-page renew prompt and tap-route to /explore-plans. On mobile a grayed card can read as merely disabled — do we add an explicit "Renew" pill/button so the action is discoverable without tapping a dimmed card, or trust the lock overlay + chip to signal tappability?
DishDetailModal → bottom-sheet on mobile: confirm we want native sheet behavior (swipe-down dismiss, grab handle, safe-area pinned Close) vs leaving the current centered dialog scaled down.

spec.primaryJobOnMobile: "Find a past plan I liked and remind myself what it was, so I can re-order it." It's a low-frequency, reference/recall surface — the user scans a list of completed subscriptions to recognize one (by plan name + date range) and glance at how it went (delivered/skipped/completion). It is NOT a daily action surface; nobody opens History to do a task, they open it to remember.
spec.currentDesktopLayoutSummary: Single centered column (maxWidth 1100). Top-to-bottom: back link → header block (uppercase eyebrow "Past plans" + DISPLAY h1 "Your subscription history." + muted description paragraph) → then a vertical flex list (gap 10) of cards, OR a centered empty-state card. Each card is a 2-column CSS grid `1fr auto`: left = PlanGlyph + clean plan name (16px) over a date range "start → end" (12px muted); right = a horizontal flex row of three right-aligned Stat blocks (Delivered "n/total", Skipped "n", Completion "n%" in brand orange). Existing mobile rule at max-width 640px only collapses the row grid to a single column — it does not re-think the three stats, which then stack under the name as three separate right-aligned lines.
spec.mobileOrganizingPrinciple: Recognition-first list scanning (Krug/Nielsen + JTBD): make every row a single glanceable line item where the plan name and date range own the row, and the three numeric stats compress into one tight horizontal metrics strip beneath the name — never three stacked right-aligned lines. Maximize rows-per-screen so the user can scan their whole history without endless scrolling; reserve emphasis (size/orange) only for the completion percentage that signals "this plan went well."

elements.name: Back link (history-back, ArrowLeft + 'Back to dashboard')
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Inline-flex uppercase 12px muted link with 13px arrow icon, 6px vertical padding, hover darkens to --ds-fg.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep, but ensure the tap target is a full 44px-high hit area (current 6px padding around a 12px label is too short for touch). Keep the label text — 'Back to dashboard' is a clear signifier; an icon-only chevron would be recall-not-recognition. Pin nothing; it scrolls with content at the very top.
elements.reorganization: Stays top-left, first element. Increase hit area to 44px min-height (pad vertically, not visually larger text). No hover-only affordance — color state must not be the only feedback on touch.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics: 44px tap targets and don't-make-me-think back navigation; HIG safe-area/thumb concerns are minor since it's a secondary control near the top.

elements.name: Header block — eyebrow 'Past plans' + h1 'Your subscription history.' + description paragraph
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Eyebrow 11px uppercase 0.18em tracked muted; h1 DISPLAY clamp(28-40px) at lineHeight 1.1; description 14px muted, 1.6 line-height, capped at 56ch.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~22-28% of viewport if left as-is (h1 wraps to 2 lines + 3-line description)
elements.densityRecommendation: Compress hard. The clamp floor of 28px h1 + 56ch description is desktop breathing room that eats the first screen on a phone. Drop h1 to ~22-24px, shorten or drop the description sentence (it's explanatory chrome, not content). Keep the eyebrow as the section label. The description's only value-add clause is 'Useful for re-ordering an old favorite' — keep that, cut 'with delivery and skip totals' since the stats are visible in every row anyway.
elements.reorganization: Stays top, below back link, but shrinks from ~3 vertical zones to ~2 tight lines so the first actual history row appears within first-glance (~700px). Remove the 56ch max-width (irrelevant under 390px) and let it use full column width.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI density + JTBD: on a phone the job is to reach the list fast; oversized type and a full descriptive paragraph are vertical cost the header hasn't earned. Hierarchy is preserved by keeping eyebrow→title→(trimmed) caption order, just smaller.

elements.name: Empty-state card ('No past plans yet.' + sub-copy)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Centered glass card, 40px/28px padding, radius-md, soft shadow; 16px bold heading + 13px muted sub-line.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep as a single centered card but reduce padding (40px top/bottom is desktop-generous) to ~28px/20px. Copy is fine. Optionally add a low-emphasis link to the active plan / menu so the empty state isn't a dead end — but only if product wants it; not required.
elements.reorganization: Occupies the list region when plans.length === 0. Stays full-width minus page padding, centered text. No structural change beyond tighter padding.
elements.rationale: Norman/visibility of status: the empty state already closes the gulf of evaluation ('it'll show up here when your plan ends'). It just needs to not feel oversized on a small screen.

elements.name: History row card (history-row) — container
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Glass card, grid 1fr/auto, gap 24, padding 20px/24px, radius-md, soft shadow; left column name+dates, right column the three stats.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: With current 640px rule (single column, stats stacked) each row balloons to ~18-22% of viewport — only ~4 rows visible. That's the core problem.
elements.densityRecommendation: Redesign the row as a compact stacked block, NOT the naive grid-collapse. Top line: PlanGlyph + plan name (16px, the recognition anchor). Second line: date range (12px muted, tnum). Third line: a single horizontal metrics strip with the three stats laid left-to-right and LEFT-aligned (Delivered · Skipped · Completion) — not three right-aligned stacked lines. Tighten padding to ~14px/16px and gap. Target ~6 rows on a 390x844 screen.
elements.reorganization: Drop the `1fr auto` two-column model entirely on mobile; rebuild as vertical: name → dates → metrics strip. The existing `grid-template-columns: 1fr` 640px rule should be replaced because it leaves the three stats as right-aligned stacked lines (awkward, wasteful). Make stats left-aligned in a flex row under the dates.
elements.rationale: JTBD + Refactoring-UI density: the row IS the surface's content; every wasted pixel per row costs a row off the screen. Recognition (name+date) leads; metrics support. The current grid collapse violates the density principle and creates ragged right-aligned numbers.

elements.name: Stat block (Stat: Delivered / Skipped / Completion)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Right-aligned; 10px uppercase 0.18em muted label above a DISPLAY 18px value (tnum); Completion value in brand orange (OG #f57f20) via `accent`.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: As-is (stacked, right-aligned) each stat is its own ~3-line zone — three of them dominate the row.
elements.densityRecommendation: Convert from three right-aligned vertical blocks into ONE compact horizontal strip: three label/value pairs side by side, left-aligned, evenly spaced (e.g. flex with gap, or label-inline 'Delivered 12/20'). Shrink value type to ~14-15px on mobile (18px DISPLAY is desktop scale). Keep Completion in orange as the single colored accent — but DO NOT rely on color alone for meaning; the 'Completion' label + % already carry it, so the orange is reinforcement not a lone signal. This is the 'three metrics as a compact row' move from the governing principle.
elements.reorganization: Stats move from the card's right column into a single inline row beneath the date range, left-aligned to match the name/date column. Remove `textAlign:right`. Use label-over-value OR label-beside-value compact pairs; prefer the compact inline pair to save vertical height.
elements.rationale: Governing principle (vertical cost) + Refactoring-UI: a single metric must not own ~1/3 of the viewport; three small reference numbers belong in a tight row. Orange stays the accent ceiling and is never the only carrier of meaning (color-alone heuristic).

elements.name: PlanGlyph (per-row icon)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: 16px currentColor glyph inline before the plan name.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep inline with the name at 16px. It's a cheap recognition aid (visual mapping of plan type) and costs no extra vertical height. No change.
elements.reorganization: Stays leading the name line.
elements.rationale: Norman: a glyph reinforces the conceptual model / recognition of which plan this was, at zero vertical cost.

proposedMobileScanOrder: Header block (eyebrow + compressed h1 + trimmed one-line caption)
History row card 1 (name+glyph → date range → compact metrics strip)
History row card N … (or Empty-state card if no plans)
spec.crossCuttingNotes: The compact metrics-strip pattern (three small label/value pairs in one left-aligned horizontal row, with one orange accent value, tnum figures) is highly reusable — it's the same density problem as any per-item stats elsewhere on the dashboard (plan/usage cards, the active-subscription summary). Define it once as a shared mobile component rather than re-collapsing each desktop grid. The 44px-min back-link hit area and the "shrink DISPLAY h1 from its clamp floor on mobile" header treatment recur on every secondary dashboard surface (Referrals, Dorm Wars sub-pages, etc.). The Stat component should grow a `dense`/mobile variant rather than being re-styled per page. Note all colors flow through --ds-* CSS vars and flip in dark mode, so any mobile restyle must use the same vars (no hard-coded hex) to keep dark-mode parity.
openDecisions: Header caption: trim to the single 're-order an old favorite' clause, or drop the description paragraph entirely on mobile? (affects how soon the first row appears).
Metrics strip layout: label-over-value (taller, matches desktop Stat) vs label-beside-value inline pairs like 'Delivered 12/20' (shortest, densest)? Pick one for the mobile Stat variant.

Should a tapped history row do anything? Rows are currently non-interactive. Given the JTBD is 're-order an old favorite,' product may want each row to be a tappable affordance (open a re-order CTA / bottom sheet). If not, confirm rows stay purely informational so we don't add false tap signifiers.
Empty state: leave as a dead-end informational card, or add a low-emphasis link to the active plan/menu so a user with no history isn't stranded?
Target rows-per-screen: confirm ~6 on 390x844 is the density goal so we can size padding/type accordingly.

spec.primaryJobOnMobile: Check and correct the few facts the kitchen relies on — "is my WhatsApp verified, what do you cook for me, where do you deliver" — and fix any that are wrong (verify WhatsApp, change email/password, edit meal preferences). It is a low-frequency settings/verification surface, not a daily-glance dashboard.
spec.currentDesktopLayoutSummary: Single centered column, maxWidth 760, padding clamp(20-40px). Vertical stack: (1) Header eyebrow + "Your profile." H1; (2) Avatar/identity TIER_POP card (dark NV gradient, 64px avatar + name/email/CID, padding 28, horizontal flex); (3) SecuritySection TIER1 card with 3 stacked rows (Email / Password / WhatsApp), each a horizontal flex of icon + label/value + status badge + pill action button, separated by dividers; (4) Account details TIER2 card with an "Edit details" toggle, a 2-col grid (Customer ID / Member since) then a divider then a 2-col grid (Full name / Dorm), flipping to a stacked input form when editing; (5) optional pending-preferences banner (orange) OR promoted banner (green); (6) Meal preferences TIER1 card with header + "Edit preferences" button and a read-only auto-fit grid (Meal type / Delivery week / Spice / Allergens / optional veg-day chips); (7) "Made with heart in Dubai" footer. Two full-screen modals (Edit preferences; and Security's Email/Password/WhatsApp via ModalShell) center on a blurred backdrop. Only existing mobile rule: .profile-grid-2 collapses to 1 column at 640px.
spec.mobileOrganizingPrinciple: Verification status first, edit-on-demand everything else. Lead with what could be wrong and block deliveries (WhatsApp/email verification badges), compress everything read-only into tight scannable rows, and push every form into bottom sheets so the page itself stays a calm status list. We have height, so stacking is fine — but no single read-only fact should eat a third of the viewport.

elements.name: Header (Eyebrow "My Account" + H1 "Your profile.")
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Eyebrow + clamp(28-38px) 700-weight H1 with orange period, marginBottom 32, framer fade-in.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep but shrink: cap H1 at ~26px, drop marginBottom from 32 to ~16, keep the eyebrow. This is pure wayfinding — it earns a line, not a third of the fold.
elements.reorganization: Same position (top), reduced vertical footprint. Consider merging visually with the identity card below since both are 'who am I' chrome.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI density: a title is hierarchy, not content; on a phone the spacing scale must contract. JTBD: nobody opens settings to read the word 'profile'.

elements.name: Avatar + identity card (TIER_POP)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Dark NV-gradient card, padding 28, horizontal flex: 64px gradient-initials avatar + name(22/800) + email(12) + CID pill.
elements.densityRecommendation: Compress padding 28->18 and shrink avatar to ~48px. Keep the horizontal layout (avatar left, name/email/CID stacked right) — do NOT center-stack it into a tall hero; that would triple its height for zero added value. CID pill stays inline under email.
elements.reorganization: Same position; tighter. The dark TIER_POP treatment stays (intentional focal 'passport' moment, and not a theme-darkening violation since it's one card).
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI: identity is recognition, give it presence but not a full fold. Norman conceptual model: this is the user's 'passport' anchor — keep it recognizable, just denser.

elements.name: Security & verification card (TIER1 wrapper)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: TIER1 card, padding 24, blue-tinted border, eyebrow 'Security & verification', 3 SecurityRows + dividers.
elements.densityRecommendation: This is the highest-priority block on mobile and should sit directly under the identity card (promote ABOVE Account details). Keep as a single card; reduce padding 24->16. The value here is the at-a-glance verified/unverified state.
elements.reorganization: Move up the scan order so the first thing after identity is 'are my channels verified'. The verification status is the page's real status signal.
elements.rationale: JTBD + UX visibility-of-status: the #1 reason to open this page is to confirm/fix WhatsApp + email verification (deliveries depend on it). Lead with it.

elements.name: SecurityRow (Email / Password / WhatsApp) — shared row component
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Horizontal flex: 36px icon tile + label/value block (minWidth 160) + StatusBadge + pill action button with ChevronRight; flexWrap allowed; 14px vertical padding; value has wordBreak break-all (long emails).
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Each row ~10-14% (more when it wraps; a long email + badge + button can wrap to 3 lines, ~18%)
elements.densityRecommendation: Re-author for narrow width instead of relying on flexWrap (which currently produces ragged 2-3 line rows). Proposed: row = icon + (label/value stacked) on line 1 with the StatusBadge right-aligned on the same line; the action becomes a full-width-feeling tap target — either the whole row is tappable (chevron affordance, opens the sheet) OR a compact pill on its own line. Ensure 44px min tap height (icon tile is 36px; expand the hit area). Keep value wordBreak for long emails. Password row: keep the enlarged dots but it needs no badge (StatusBadge returns null for 'set') — fine.
elements.reorganization: From 'icon + value + badge + button' all on one horizontal line to a 2-tier row: top line label+status, second line value, with the entire row as the trigger (recognition over recall; chevron already signals 'opens detail').
elements.rationale: iOS HIG native list pattern + 44px targets; UX no-hover-on-touch (current hover-only bg change on .security-action-btn must not be the only affordance); Refactoring-UI: stop the wrap-induced ragged height.

elements.name: StatusBadge (Verified / Unverified / Not set)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Pill with shield icon + label; success-wash green / amber #c89417 / neutral; returns null for password 'set'.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep prominent and right-aligned on each row's first line. Never color-alone — it already pairs ShieldCheck/ShieldAlert icon + text label, which satisfies the HIG/Norman requirement; preserve that. This is the single most valuable pixel on the surface.
elements.reorganization: Pin to the right edge of the row's top line so the eye can scan a vertical column of badges down the card.
elements.rationale: UX visibility-of-status + don't-make-me-think: the whole job is reading these three states at a glance; iOS HIG never-color-alone (already satisfied — keep icon+label).

elements.name: Account details card (TIER2) — read-only context + edit toggle
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: TIER2 card padding 24; header eyebrow + 'Edit details' pill; 2-col grid (Customer ID / Member since); divider; 2-col grid (Full name / Dorm); flips to stacked input form on edit.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~35% of viewport read-only (grids collapse to 1-col at 640, so 4 stacked Fields + divider)
elements.densityRecommendation: Demote below Security. The 4 Fields currently each take a full row at 640px (label 10px + value 14px) — that's tall for low-value data. Render the read-only facts as a compact 2-up grid that survives below 640 (Customer ID + Member since as a tight pair; Full name + Dorm as a pair) rather than 1-per-row, OR keep 1-col but tighten gap 20->12. Customer ID + Member since are reference-only; they don't each deserve a full row of breathing space.
elements.reorganization: Position drops (after Security). Keep the 'Edit details' gate. Strong consideration: move the edit FORM into a bottom sheet rather than inline-expanding the card, to match the rest of the surface's sheet pattern (see Open Decisions).

elements.name: Account details — inline Edit form (Full name input + Dorm select + Cancel/Save)

On mobile, present this edit state as a bottom sheet (consistent with meal-prefs + security flows) so the user isn't editing a form wedged mid-page with the keyboard covering the Save button. Pin Cancel/Save to the bottom of the sheet in thumb reach.

elements.name: Pending-preferences banner (orange 'From next plan' diff list)

But tighten: padding 14/18->12, and let each diff line wrap cleanly (it already has flexWrap with a 110px min label — reduce that min on narrow screens so old->new doesn't orphan). The 'Discard' link must be a real 44px tap target, not a 4px-padded underline.

elements.name: Promoted banner (green 'New meal preferences applied')

elements.name: Meal preferences card (TIER1) — header + 'Edit preferences' CTA
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: TIER1 card, orange-tinted border, padding 24; header block (eyebrow + helper sentence maxWidth 460) on the left, orange 'Edit preferences' pill on the right (flexWrap).

elements.name: Meal preferences — read-only value grid (Meal type / Delivery week / Spice / Allergens / optional veg-day chips)

Veg-day chips span full width as a final row when present. Tighten inner padding 18->12, gap 18->10.

elements.name: Save-state inline toasts (account 'Details saved' / 'Preferences saved' / 'Saved for next subscription' / 'Pending changes discarded')
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Small inline success/neutral wash chips appended under their respective cards, auto-clear after 2.5-4s.

elements.rationale: Microinteractions immediate-feedback + UX visibility-of-status; these are correct as-is, just verify no layout jank on small screens.

elements.name: Edit Preferences modal (meal prefs) — Meal pref select, Delivery-week toggle, religious veg-day picker, Allergen chips, Spice select, Cancel/Save
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Center modal maxWidth 520 on blurred backdrop, padding 28, maxHeight calc(100vh-48px) scroll; close X top-right; eyebrow + 'Update what we cook for you.' title + forward-looking note; stacked fields incl. week-type toggle (flex 1 1 200px), veg-day grid (repeat(W) columns), allergen pill wrap, spice select; Cancel/Save flex row.
elements.densityRecommendation: Convert from center-card modal to a bottom sheet that rises to ~92vh with a grab handle and a sticky footer holding Cancel/Save (the long 'Save for next subscription' label needs the bottom anchored so it survives keyboard + scroll). Week-type toggle: keep 2 buttons but let them go full-width-stacked under ~360px (flex 1 1 200px currently forces side-by-side that's cramped). Veg-day grid (repeat(W) cols across) is fine at W=5/6 if each cell stays >=44px wide; on 360px verify 6 cells fit or wrap to two rows. Allergen pills already wrap — good.
elements.reorganization: Center modal -> bottom sheet; primary action sticky at bottom in thumb reach; backdrop tap-to-close preserved (already !isPending guarded).
elements.rationale: iOS HIG bottom-sheet for forms + safe-area + thumb-reach; Microinteractions progressive disclosure (dense edit detail belongs in a sheet, not on the page).

elements.name: Security ModalShell modals — Change Email / Change Password / WhatsApp Verify
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Shared ModalShell: center card maxWidth 460, blurred backdrop, Esc-to-close, close X, title + subtitle, body fields; Email (resend-verify button when unverified + new-email input); Password (current/new/confirm PasswordInputs with eye toggles + live 5-rule checklist + 'email me a reset link'); WhatsApp (2-stage: number -> 6-digit code, resend link).
elements.densityRecommendation: Same as meal-prefs: render as bottom sheets with sticky Cancel/primary footer. Password sheet is the tallest (3 inputs + 5-rule checklist) — ensure it scrolls within the sheet and the Update button stays pinned. Inputs are already 44-48px; eye toggle is 32px (acceptable but nudge toward 44px hit area). WhatsApp code input (numeric, one-time-code, centered tracking) is good — keep inputMode numeric so the number pad opens.
elements.reorganization: Center modals -> bottom sheets, consistent with the meal-prefs sheet, so all three security flows feel native. Keep the secondary 'reset link' / 'resend code' links below the action row but give them 44px tap height.
