elements.name: 'Made with heart in Dubai' footer
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Centered uppercase 11px caption with orange heart, padding 16.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep, unchanged — it's the natural scroll terminus and signals 'end of page'. No vertical cost worth fighting.
elements.reorganization: Stays last. Acts as a scroll-end signifier.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI/Norman: a quiet end-cap gives closure to the scroll; harmless and brand-warm.

proposedMobileScanOrder: Meal preferences card (header + full-width Edit CTA)
Account details card (compressed read-only + Edit details)
Made with heart in Dubai footer
spec.crossCuttingNotes: Bottom-sheet pattern is the big reusable win: this surface has FOUR modals (meal-prefs + the three ModalShell security flows) that should all become bottom sheets with a sticky thumb-reach footer and safe-area padding — build one shared MobileSheet wrapper and the whole dashboard's modals can adopt it. The 44px tap-target audit recurs everywhere: SecurityRow action pill, 'Discard these changes' underline (currently 4px padding), the eye-toggle (32px), and the password-reset/resend text links all need bigger hit areas. Hover-only signifiers (.security-action-btn and .prefs-edit-btn hover bg/border) must not be the sole affordance on touch — give touch a persistent resting style. The compress-low-value-reference-data move (Account details 2-up grid, meal-prefs 2-across) is a pattern other dashboard surfaces with stat grids will reuse. StatusBadge already pairs icon+label (never color-alone) — reuse that contract for any status pill elsewhere. Orange stays the ceiling (#f57f20) for the pending banner and all primary CTAs; the dark TIER_POP identity card is a deliberate single-card focal moment, not a theme darkening, so it's safe.
openDecisions: Should the Account-details edit form become a bottom sheet (consistent with every other edit on this surface) or stay an inline card-expansion? Sheet is more consistent but the inline expand is lighter-weight for a 2-field edit.

Promote Security ABOVE Account details on mobile (recommended — verification is the primary job), or preserve the current desktop order. Desktop already renders identity -> Security -> Account details, so this is really 'confirm we keep Security second and don't let Account details creep up'.

For the meal-prefs read-only grid on small Android (360px), is a forced 2-across acceptable for the longer values like 'Mon–Sat (6 days)', or should Delivery week get a full-width row while Spice/Meal-type/Allergens stay 2-across?
Make the entire SecurityRow tappable (whole-row trigger, iOS-list style) vs. keeping a discrete pill button — whole-row is more thumb-friendly but removes the explicit button signifier.
Adopt a single shared MobileSheet component now (refactor all four modals) or ship sheet behavior per-modal first — affects scope/effort.

The meal-prefs helper sentence and modal forward-looking note are long for a phone; trim to one short line on mobile, or keep full copy (the 'changes apply from next subscription' message is load-bearing for the kitchen-contract mental model, so don't cut its meaning).

spec.primaryJobOnMobile: "Get a human to help me right now, with the least friction." A student on a phone opens Support because something is wrong or unclear (a meal, a charge, an allergy, "do you deliver to me?"). The job is: either self-serve the answer fast (FAQ) or punch through to a live channel (WhatsApp first, email second), with their Account reference handy so the conversation starts warm. On a phone, "reach a human" beats "read my account card."
spec.currentDesktopLayoutSummary: Single centered column (maxWidth 1400). Order: motion header (eyebrow + "We're here for you." + dynamic subline) → "Get in touch" section as a 3-across grid (Account info on TIER_POP / accent border, Email on TIER2, WhatsApp on TIER2 + green border), each card minHeight 260 → "Common questions" section: one TIER2 panel containing 8 collapsed FAQItem rows → centered "Made with heart in Dubai" footer. The only existing responsive rule is `@media (max-width:1024px){ .support-grid { 1fr } }`, which stacks the three contact cards vertically — a pure reflow, not a mobile reorganization.
spec.mobileOrganizingPrinciple: Channels first, reference second, answers third. Lead with "how do I reach you" as a tight, thumb-reachable action block (WhatsApp the clear primary), demote the Account-info reference to a compact collapsible strip (it's recall-support, not the action), and give the FAQ the most vertical room since self-serve deflects most contacts. Drop desktop's three 260px equal cards — that's the single biggest vertical-cost offender on a phone (Jobs-to-be-Done + Refactoring-UI density).

elements.name: motion.header (Eyebrow + h1 "We're here for you." + dynamic subline)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Eyebrow kicker, clamp(24–30px) bold h1 with orange period, 15px muted subline that swaps to "{N} dinners delivered" when totalDelivered >= 5; marginBottom 36.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep but compress: pin h1 to the low end (~22–24px), tighten marginBottom 36 → ~20, cap subline at 2 lines. Keep the dynamic "{N} dinners delivered" line — it's cheap warmth and reassurance ("reply within 15 min" is a status signal). Drop the eyebrow only if vertical pressure forces it; otherwise keep at 11px.
elements.reorganization: Stays at top but shorter. The 15-min reply-time promise should survive in the subline because it sets the expectation that drives the channel choice below it.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI (constrained spacing, hierarchy by size) + Influence (social-proof "N dinners" + status "15 min"). Desktop's 36px breathing room is luxury a phone can't afford above the action block.

elements.name: "Get in touch" section eyebrow + hairline divider
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Eyebrow "Get in touch" with a flex:1 1px hairline running to the right edge; marginBottom 14.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep as a thin section label; the hairline rhythm is fine and cheap. Could be relabeled "Reach us" for directness but not required.
elements.reorganization: Unchanged in role; sits directly above the contact actions.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics: a lightweight signifier of section boundaries aids scanning. Costs almost nothing vertically.

elements.name: WhatsApp contact card (TIER2 + green border, MessageCircle icon, "Fastest · ~15 min" eyebrow, "Open WhatsApp →" CTA)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Third card in the grid, minHeight 260, 44px green icon tile, eyebrow, h1-style title, 13px body, solid #25D366 pill CTA with green shadow.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~31% of viewport each (three stacked = nearly 3 screens today)
elements.densityRecommendation: Promote to the visual primary and SHRINK the shell. Kill minHeight 260. Render as a compact full-width row: small green icon + "Chat on WhatsApp / Fastest · ~15 min" stacked on the left, full-width (or right-aligned) solid green CTA pill at >=44px tap height. Drop or trim the "Available 7 AM–9 PM, 7 days" line to one short line. This is THE action; it should be the most prominent thing below the header.
elements.reorganization: Moves from grid-position-3 to FIRST in the contact block. Becomes a horizontal action row, not a 260px card. CTA pill should be wide and thumb-reachable.
elements.rationale: Jobs-to-be-Done (fastest path to a human is the job) + iOS HIG (primary action, large tap target) + brand: green is the locked WhatsApp vocabulary, keep it.

elements.name: Email contact card (TIER2, Mail icon, "Within 24 hours" eyebrow, mailto CTA showing SUPPORT_EMAIL)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Second card, minHeight 260, orange-tint 44px icon tile, eyebrow, title "Email us", 13px body, ghost orange pill whose label is the full email address (truncates with ellipsis).
elements.densityRecommendation: Demote to a compact secondary row beneath WhatsApp. Kill minHeight 260 and the 44px icon tile (shrink to ~28px or inline icon). The CTA label is the email string — on a 360px screen that truncates ugly; instead label the pill "Email us" and show the address as a small line below, or keep mailto with a fixed "Email support" label. Trim the "billing/paper trail" descriptor to a half-line.
elements.reorganization: Second in the stacked contact block, visually lighter than WhatsApp (ghost pill stays, no green). Forms a 2-row contact pair with WhatsApp.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI (de-emphasize the slower channel via lighter treatment) + UX-Heuristics (the email-as-button-label truncation breaks recognition on narrow screens).

elements.name: Account info card (TIER_POP accent, "Your reference" eyebrow, Name/Email/ID rows, "Quote your ID" hint)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: First card, the only TIER_POP/data card, minHeight 260, three label-value rows (ID in MONO) with hairline separators, footer hint "Quote your ID so we can pull up your account instantly."
elements.densityRecommendation: Demote and collapse. On desktop it leads because it's the spotlight data card; on mobile it's reference you consult, not an action. Render as a compact collapsed strip/disclosure: a single TIER_POP bar reading "Your reference · ID {cid}" with a tap-to-expand revealing Name / Email / full ID. Keep the ID prominent and the one-tap-copy affordance worth adding (copy the ID). Keep the "Quote your ID" hint inside the expanded state only.
elements.reorganization: Moves from grid-position-1 (desktop lead) to AFTER the two contact rows, as a collapsible reference strip. Position/importance preserved but size drastically cut. Consider a copy-to-clipboard tap on the ID since users will paste it into WhatsApp.
elements.rationale: Jobs-to-be-Done (reference supports the action, it isn't the action) + Microinteractions (progressive disclosure into a strip; add copy feedback) + Norman (mapping: the ID lives next to the channels where you'll quote it).

elements.name: "Common questions" section eyebrow + hairline divider
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Eyebrow "Common questions" + flex:1 hairline; marginBottom 14.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep as-is; cheap section signifier introducing the self-serve block.
elements.reorganization: Unchanged role, sits above the FAQ accordion.
elements.rationale: UX-Heuristics: section labeling aids scanning of long lists.

elements.name: FAQ accordion (TIER2 panel wrapping 8 FAQItem rows)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: One TIER2 panel, clamp(20–28px) padding, containing 8 collapsible FAQItem rows (18px vertical padding each, 14px question, + rotates to x, 13px answer at lineHeight 1.65).

Reduce the outer panel padding (clamp low end ~16px) so questions use full width. Verify each tappable row header is >=44px (currently 18+18 padding + ~17px text ≈ 53px — good). Optionally reorder the 8 to put the most phone-urgent first ("Can I skip a meal?", "When is my meal delivered?", "Do you deliver to my dorm?") since those map to time-sensitive panic moments.

elements.rationale: Microinteractions (progressive disclosure is correct here) + iOS HIG (native list/accordion) + Jobs-to-be-Done (self-serve deflection; reorder by phone-urgent intent). This block legitimately earns vertical space.

elements.name: "Made with heart in Dubai" footer
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Centered, 11px uppercase letter-spaced text with inline orange-filled Heart icon; 16px vertical padding.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep verbatim; it's a small warmth signature with negligible cost. No change.
elements.reorganization: Stays last, after the FAQ. Ensure it clears the bottom safe-area inset.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI (a quiet brand grace note; deliberately low in hierarchy) + iOS HIG (respect safe-area at the page bottom).

spec.crossCuttingNotes: The "three equal cards, minHeight 260, stack to 1fr under 1024px" pattern is the recurring vertical-cost trap across the dashboard — the same reflow-not-reorganize move likely appears on Plan and elsewhere. The mobile fix (collapse equal cards into a prioritized vertical stack where one item is clearly primary and the rest shrink to compact rows) is reusable. The FAQItem accordion and Eyebrow+hairline section header are shared `_shared` components and already mobile-appropriate; any padding/tap-target tuning done here should be made breakpoint-aware in the shared components so Plan's FAQ benefits too. The collapsible "reference strip + copy ID" treatment is reusable for any account/ID display elsewhere (Profile). WhatsApp green primary CTA + ghost-orange secondary is an established channel-vocabulary pair worth standardizing as the mobile contact-row component. Note: `data-tooltip` ("Opens WhatsApp", "Opens your email app") is hover-only and invisible on touch — drop or convert to visible sub-labels on mobile (UX-Heuristics: no hover-only info on touch).
openDecisions: Account info on mobile: collapsed reference strip (tap to expand) vs. always-visible compact two-line block? Strip saves ~25% viewport but adds a tap before the user can read their ID.
Should we add a copy-to-clipboard affordance on the customer ID? It maps directly to "quote your ID in WhatsApp," but it's net-new interaction not in the current code.
Reorder the 8 FAQS array for phone-urgent intent (skip / delivery time / dorm coverage first) vs. keep the current author-curated order? Reordering changes desktop too unless gated.
Email CTA label: keep the full email address as the button text (truncates on 360px) or relabel the pill "Email us" with the address shown as a small caption line below?

Does the dynamic "{N} dinners delivered" subline survive on first-glance mobile, or is the generic "Real humans, real food" line preferred to save a line of height for low-delivery users (it already branches at totalDelivered >= 5)?

spec.primaryJobOnMobile: "Did I earn anything, and how do I earn more right now?" — a Premium subscriber opens the hub on their phone to (a) see their wallet/streak status, (b) fire off the one action that earns AED (Send a Free Meal to a friend over WhatsApp), and (c) glance at how close they are to the next reward. It is a motivation-and-action surface, not a data dashboard.
spec.currentDesktopLayoutSummary: Single dark, full-bleed scroll column inside a flex container (padding clamp 16-24 / 20-32, gap 16). Vertical order: optional CelebrationBanner -> optional DoublerActiveBanner -> TopChrome (one flex row: progression block left, wallet+streak chips right, flex-wraps) -> HeroCTA (centered tagline + big pill button + helper text + next-milestone pill) -> 3-column progress grid (.hub-progress-grid: CycleColumn / LifetimeColumn / SideRewardsColumn at repeat(3,1fr), collapsing to 2-up <1024 and 1-up <768) -> 2-column lower row (.hub-activity-grid: ActivityFeed 1.1fr / ScoutsStrip 1fr, 1-up <768). Everything else (Quests, Ladder, Streak Chest, Squad, Wallet, Progression, Google Review, Weekly/Monthly chooser, side-quest info) is a centered Modal sheet. A first-visit DormWarsTour spotlights the three columns + streak chip. PremiumGateOverlay frosts the whole thing for ineligible plans.
spec.mobileOrganizingPrinciple: Status then action then progress: compress the identity/money/streak chrome into a tight 3-row glanceable header (identity line, then a Wallet|Streak 2-across metric row), give the single earn action (Send a Free Meal) and the tappable earn-now Side Quests prime first/second-fold space, and demote the slow-moving progress bars, squad, and social feed below — pushing every dense detail into bottom sheets so the scrollable surface stays light and thumb-driven.

elements.name: PremiumGateOverlay
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Full-screen fixed dialog (z-9000) frosting the SSR hub; centered card maxWidth 460 with lock eyebrow, 24px headline, sub copy, a 2-column perk teaser grid (6 perks), and an upgrade CTA. Only shown to non-Premium plans.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Full viewport (it is a takeover) for ineligible users; zero for eligible users
elements.densityRecommendation: For ineligible users this IS the surface — keep it. The 2-up perk grid (repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))) is fine at 390px but tighten to a single column at <=360px so each perk's label+sub never truncates. Pin the upgrade CTA to the bottom safe-area within the card so it's in thumb reach without scrolling past 6 perks; the card already scrolls (overflowY auto on backdrop).
elements.reorganization: Stays a full-screen sheet. Card goes width:100% with 16px side gutters; perk grid 2-up at 390 / 1-up at 360; CTA sticky to card bottom.
elements.rationale: JTBD + iOS HIG: for these users the only job is decide-to-upgrade, so the offer and its single CTA must be reachable without hunting. This is the dominant first-glance state for the segment that sees it.

elements.name: CelebrationBanner
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Conditional role=status bar at very top: gradient wash by accent, headline (16px/900) + sub line with inline wallet figure, dismiss X (32px circle), auto-dismiss 14s, slide-in animation.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~12-15% when present (two text lines + padding); 0% otherwise
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep but cap to two lines and let the sub line wrap/ellipsis; ensure the 32px X grows to a 44px tap target via padding. Do not let the headline+sub push the wallet/CTA below the fold — it is transient (14s) so it can overlay rather than shove content, but simplest is to keep it inline and accept the one-time cost.
elements.reorganization: Full-bleed top banner, same position. Headline 15px, sub 12px, X gets 44px hit area. Stacks naturally; no layout change beyond tap-target.
elements.rationale: Microinteractions (Saffer) + visibility of status: this is the immediate-feedback payoff for earning. High emotional value, so it earns first-glance space, but it is ephemeral so it must not permanently cost height.

elements.name: DoublerActiveBanner
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Conditional role=status pill-bar under celebration: Zap icon + '2x rewards active' + countdown remaining, gold gradient wash.
elements.densityRecommendation: Compress to a single line: '2x active · {time} left' with the Zap glyph; drop the secondary explanatory clause ('Cash for invites + cycle milestones doubled for') on mobile — it's the kind of dense detail that belongs in the chest sheet, not a status strip. One line, ~36px tall.
elements.reorganization: Single-line full-bleed strip. Truncate explanatory copy; keep glyph + state + countdown only.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI density: a time-bound status bar should be one glanceable line on a phone. The 'why' is recall-able from the Streak Chest sheet; recognition over recall says show the state, hide the explanation.

elements.name: TopChrome — Progression block (avatar + ring + title)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Clickable pill: 46px progress-ring-wrapped tier avatar glyph + eyebrow ('N to NextTitle' / 'Apex Tier') + 18px title + optional Early Access / GOAT badges. Opens Progression modal.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep the avatar+ring (the identity hook) but shrink avatar to ~38px and demote the eyebrow/title to a single tight line beside it. The progression block can stay full-width as row 1 of the chrome, with wallet+streak as a compact 2-up row directly beneath, rather than all three trying to share one wrapping flex line. Badges (Early Access/GOAT) move to a single inline chip; if both present, GOAT wins and Early Access folds into the Progression sheet.
elements.reorganization: Becomes the top identity row, full-width, left-aligned: avatar + title + next-step eyebrow on one line. No longer competes horizontally with the money chips.
elements.rationale: Norman conceptual model + Octalysis status: identity/progress is the emotional anchor and should lead, but it is not the job — so it gets one tight row, not a third of the screen. Avatar+ring is the recognizable signifier worth keeping.

elements.name: TopChrome — Wallet chip
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Clickable pill: CoinIcon(26) + 'WALLET' eyebrow + 'AED {n}' (18px/900) + optional '+{pending}'. Opens Wallet history modal.
elements.densityRecommendation: This is the single most important number on the surface — pair it with the streak chip as a compact 2-across row directly under the identity line (the code comment already says these two 'read as a matched pair'). Keep AED value at 18px; keep the pending '+N' inline. Ensure 44px min height.
elements.reorganization: Half-width chip in a 2-up status row (Wallet | Streak), sitting under the identity row. Tap opens the existing Wallet sheet.
elements.rationale: JTBD: 'did I earn anything' is answered by this number — it must be visible before any scroll. Refactoring-UI: two metrics across one row is the textbook fix for a single metric eating a third of a phone viewport.

elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Clickable pill: tier-colored Flame(22) + 'STREAK' eyebrow + '{n}d' + gift disc (pulsing/haloed when chestReady). Opens Streak Chest modal.

The 'chest ready' pulsing gift is a high-value variable-reward trigger — preserve its glow/halo state since it drives a tap into the chest. Do not rely on color alone for 'ready': keep the gift-disc fill + ring so it reads on a glance.
elements.reorganization: Half-width chip paired with Wallet. Tap opens Streak Chest sheet.
elements.rationale: Hooked/Octalysis: the streak + ready-chest is the daily-return trigger. Pairing it with wallet keeps both money signals on one compact row (Refactoring-UI density) while preserving the discoverable 'open me' signifier (Saffer).

elements.name: HeroCTA — 'Send a Free Meal' button + tagline + helper + next-milestone pill
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Centered section: tagline ('Earn AED 20 every time a friend joins'), big pulsing/bobbing orange pill button (Send + label + ArrowRight, minWidth 240), helper line ('Opens WhatsApp...'), and a next-cycle-milestone hint pill ('N more recruits unlock {label}').
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~30-35% if kept as the centered 4-stack with clamp padding
elements.densityRecommendation: This element EARNS its space — it is the job. But trim the stack: keep the button (full-width pill, >=48px tall) and a one-line tagline above it; collapse the helper line into smaller supporting text or drop it (the WhatsApp behavior is self-evident on tap). The next-milestone pill is valuable motivation but is also the headline of CycleColumn below — show it once. Best: keep the button + tagline at the top of the scroll, and ALSO pin a slim version of the button to the bottom safe-area as a persistent thumb-reach action so it survives scrolling.

elements.rationale: JTBD + iOS HIG: the primary action belongs in thumb reach and must dominate. Refactoring-UI: drop redundant supporting copy; one strong CTA beats a CTA buried under three explanatory lines.

elements.name: CycleColumn (This Month — burst goals)

Whole card opens Quests modal; dots focus-open it.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: ~25-30% as a full-width card when grid collapses to 1fr
elements.densityRecommendation: Compress hard. The horizontal dot-bar barely fits 5 dots+labels at 360px (the code's own audit P1-9 notes collisions). On mobile, drop the standalone numeric-label row (the dots + the status sentence already carry the info) and keep a single progress bar + the primary 'N more recruits to {label}' line + the quiet 'X of N · Nd left' meta. Reduce card padding from 18 to ~12 (already does this <1024). The full bar with all 5 emblems can live in the Quests sheet.
elements.reorganization: Becomes a compact status card/row: eyebrow + one progress bar + 1 primary line + 1 meta line. Tapping opens the full Quests sheet for the dot detail.
elements.rationale: Refactoring-UI + UX-heuristics: a 5-stop horizontal ladder is a desktop affordance; on a phone it collides and forces hover-tooltips (no hover on touch). Progressive disclosure (Saffer) — push the granular dots into the existing Quests sheet.

elements.name: LifetimeColumn (Lifetime Path — permanent perks)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Tinted card (accent CYAN): eyebrow+Trophy, 2-line title, 44px progress bar with 4 tier dots (5%/10%+EA/Jacket/100 meals) + head marker, status body referencing current cash tier. Opens Lifetime Path (TrophyLadder) modal.
elements.densityRecommendation: Same compression as CycleColumn: one slim bar + a single 'N to next tier ({perk})' line; drop the dense per-dot labels into the Lifetime Path sheet. Lower priority than the cycle bar because lifetime tiers move slowly — it is reference, not this-session action.
elements.reorganization: Compact status row beneath CycleColumn: bar + 1 line of next-tier copy. Tap opens TrophyLadder sheet.
elements.rationale: JTBD: lifetime progress is slow-moving context, not a same-session lever, so it ranks below the cycle goal and the action. Refactoring-UI hierarchy via reduced size/weight.

elements.name: SideRewardsColumn (Side Quests — more ways to earn)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Tinted card (accent GREEN): eyebrow+Sparkles, title, a priority-sorted list of 4 rows (Google review, 4 weekly reviews, Monthly wrap, Weekly Streak Reward) each with emblem + label + status sub-line + status chip (Tap to claim / Pending / Locked / Earned / Coming soon). Actionable rows route to their action; passive rows open the info modal.
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep this as a real list (it already is one) — this is the highest-value secondary-action block after the Send CTA. Mobile-native treatment: each quest is a full-width 44px+ list row (iOS list pattern), emblem left, label+sub stacked center, status chip right. The top actionable row ('Tap to claim' Google review = instant AED) deserves visual lift to the top — the existing computeSideRewardPriority sort already does this; preserve it. This card should arguably sit HIGHER than the two progress bars on mobile because it contains tappable earn-now actions, not just progress viz.
elements.reorganization: Becomes a native list section. Consider promoting it above CycleColumn/LifetimeColumn on mobile so earn-now actions cluster near the Send CTA, leaving the slow progress bars lower.
elements.rationale: JTBD: 'how do I earn more right now' — these rows are direct earn actions (review, wrap, claim). UX-heuristics: list rows are unambiguous tap targets and the status chip gives visibility of status without color-alone (text labels present).

elements.name: ActivityFeed (Happening Now)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Tinted card (accent GREEN, empty title): one highlighted live pulse line ('{name} joined {dorm}', green dot, rotates every 4.5s) + up to 3 muted recent lines; GOAT EliteTag inline. Empty state: 'Quiet across the dorms right now.'
elements.densityRecommendation: Keep but shrink to the single rotating pulse line + at most 2 recent lines on mobile. This is social-proof ambiance (Octalysis/Influence), not an action — it belongs deep in the scroll. Do not let it occupy prime real estate. Reduce internal gap and row padding.
elements.reorganization: Stacks as a short ambient strip near the bottom of the scroll, above or paired with Squad. Trim recent items to 2.
elements.rationale: Influence-psychology (social proof) gives it a reason to exist, but JTBD ranks it last — it neither tells the user their status nor offers an action, so it sinks to deep fold.

elements.name: ScoutsStrip (Your Squad)

elements.densityRecommendation: Keep the horizontal-scroll tile pattern — it is already mobile-friendly (overflow-x auto, 64px tiles, scrollbar hidden) and is one of the few elements that does NOT need reflow. Ensure tiles are >=44px tappable (they're ~64px wide, fine). Keep the 'Send new' tile as the trailing affordance — it reinforces the primary action. This can sit just below the Hero/Side Quests since it's tied to the referral loop, but its detail (journeys) is in sheets so the strip itself stays shallow.
elements.reorganization: Horizontal scroller stays as-is; just full-width. Header shows count; tap tile -> Journey sheet, tap card header -> Squad sheet.
elements.rationale: iOS HIG horizontal card scroller is a native pattern and the existing implementation already follows it. Microinteractions: the in-line 'Send new' tile is a secondary discoverable trigger for the core action.

elements.name: DormWarsTour (first-visit walkthrough)

Skip/ESC/backdrop -> consent. Suppressed behind the Premium gate.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Full viewport overlay on first visit; 0 thereafter

The one risk: if the mobile reorg changes element order/heights, the scrollIntoView+measure spotlight must still land on the moved targets — the [data-tour] wrappers use display:contents so they survive reflow. Verify the streak-chest target (now a half-width chip in the 2-up row) still measures correctly. Tooltip Next/Finish/Skip buttons need 44px tap targets (current Next is 8px/18px padding — borderline, bump up).

elements.rationale: Norman: the tour teaches the conceptual model and is decoupled by selector, so it adapts automatically — but iOS HIG 44pt targets and the moved streak-chip measurement are the two things to re-check.

elements.name: Detail Modals (Quests, TrophyLadder, StreakChest, Squad, GoogleReview, Wallet, Progression, Weekly/Monthly chooser, QuestInfo)
elements.currentDesktopTreatment: Centered Modal component (maxWidth 640, maxHeight 88vh, overflow auto, hub-modal-in animation) holding each dense detail screen — flip-card milestone ladders, claim flows, wallet history, review choosers, etc.
elements.currentVerticalCostMobile: Full viewport when open; 0 when closed
elements.densityRecommendation: Convert the centered modal into a bottom sheet on mobile (slide up from bottom, respect safe-area, drag/swipe-to-dismiss + visible close). These sheets are where ALL the dense detail correctly lives, which is exactly why the surface chrome can be so compressed. Ensure each sheet's primary action button sits at the bottom in thumb reach and any screenshot upload / file picker (GoogleReview) and 'Don't show again' style CTAs meet 44px. maxHeight ~92vh with internal scroll.
elements.reorganization: Centered card -> bottom sheet pattern. Content inside is already scrollable; primary CTAs anchored bottom.
elements.rationale: iOS HIG + Saffer progressive disclosure: bottom sheets are the native home for depth on a phone and the mechanism that lets the always-visible hub stay light. This is the keystone that makes the whole compression strategy viable.

proposedMobileScanOrder: HeroCTA — 'Send a Free Meal' button + tagline + helper + next-milestone pill
SideRewardsColumn (Side Quests — more ways to earn)
Detail Modals (Quests, TrophyLadder, StreakChest, Squad, GoogleReview, Wallet, Progression, Weekly/Monthly chooser, QuestInfo)
spec.crossCuttingNotes: 1) The Wallet|Streak 'matched pair' chips are a reusable mobile pattern: two key metrics as a compact 2-across row under the identity line — reuse this anywhere two status metrics currently sit in a wrapping flex header (e.g. other dashboard surfaces). 2) The Column shell (tinted-glass card with eyebrow+icon+'Details' pill) is shared by 5 blocks here; defining ONE mobile rule for it — reduced padding (~12), compressed body, whole-card tap opens a bottom sheet — fixes all of them at once and likely recurs on any other card-grid surface. 3) The centered Modal -> bottom-sheet conversion is the single most reusable mobile decision; if done as a shared Modal-component change it upgrades every sheet on this surface (and elsewhere that imports it). 4) Horizontal-scroll tile strips (ScoutsStrip) are already correct mobile-native and should be the template for any 'row of small entities' elsewhere. 5) Status chips that today rely partly on color (Tap to claim / Pending / Locked / Earned) already carry text labels — keep that text on mobile (never color-alone). 6) All pulsing/bobbing CTA + ready-chest animations must keep honoring prefers-reduced-motion (already wired in HubStyles).
openDecisions: Should Side Quests (earn-now actions) be promoted ABOVE the Cycle/Lifetime progress bars on mobile? JTBD argues yes (they're tappable earn actions, the bars are passive progress viz), but it breaks the desktop left-to-right Cycle->Lifetime->Side narrative order. Product owner call on whether mobile order can diverge from desktop here.

Do we add a persistent sticky bottom 'Send a Free Meal' bar in the thumb zone, or rely on the top HeroCTA only? Sticky maximizes the primary action but adds permanent chrome and could clash with the app's existing bottom nav/tab bar if one exists.

On mobile, drop the HeroCTA helper line ('Opens WhatsApp · they eat first meal free · you earn when they subscribe')? It aids first-time recognition but costs a line every visit. Keep for new users / drop for returning?
The next-milestone hint currently appears twice (HeroCTA pill AND CycleColumn primary line). Which one wins on mobile — keep it under the CTA as motivation, or only in the Cycle card?
Convert all detail Modals to bottom sheets globally (shared component change) vs. only the Dorm Wars ones? Global is cleaner but touches other surfaces beyond this analysis's scope.

For ineligible users the PremiumGateOverlay is the entire mobile experience — is an upgrade-focused mobile layout (offer + sticky CTA) worth bespoke design effort, or is the current centered card 'good enough' since it's a conversion dead-end the user should leave quickly?

spec.surface: Shell, Nav & Modals (dashboard layout chrome: Sidebar rail/drawer, hamburger, content-border wrapper, SidebarDropdowns Now/Profile/Refer trays, MonthlyWrapForceOverlay, WeeklyReviewTakeover, MonthlyReviewTakeover)
spec.primaryJobOnMobile: Get me to the page I need (or act on a time-bound prompt) with one thumb, fast — the shell's job is wayfinding and surfacing "what needs my attention right now," not holding content. The full-screen takeovers have a secondary but distinct job: complete a multi-step review/wrap form comfortably on a phone.
spec.currentDesktopLayoutSummary: Fixed 76px icon rail pinned left (top:16/left:16/bottom:16, expands to 240px on hover) holding logo, 6 nav links, a spacer, a framed "Refer & earn" row, the "Now" tray trigger, and a profile chip at the bottom. Main content sits in a flex row with marginLeft:92 inside a cream content-border card (min-height calc(100vh-32px)). Dropdowns (Refer/Now/Profile) render as 280px floating panels anchored at left:calc(100%+8px) beside the rail. Three overlays mount globally: MonthlyWrapForceOverlay (centered 480px card on a navy radial-glow scrim) and two full-screen takeovers (WeeklyReviewTakeover 5 steps, MonthlyReviewTakeover 8/4 steps) at inset:0 with a header (back chip + step counter + reward chip + close X), a centered main column (max-width 560-820px), and a footer "Save & continue later". At ≤1024px the rail already converts to an off-canvas 280px drawer (translateX) opened by a fixed 44px hamburger top-left, content marginLeft:0 + 8px padding.
spec.mobileOrganizingPrinciple: The shell must vacate the screen and live at the thumb. On a phone, navigation is not a persistent rail — it is a bottom-anchored layer summoned on demand. Replace the top-left hamburger + side drawer mental model with thumb-reachable triggers: a bottom tab bar (or bottom-summoned sheet) for nav, the Now tray as a bottom sheet, and the takeovers as full-height step flows whose primary CTA is pinned to the bottom safe area. Every chrome element earns zero permanent vertical cost on content pages; it appears only when invoked.

elements.densityRecommendation: Replace the off-canvas full-height drawer with a persistent bottom tab bar (~56px + safe-area) holding the 3-4 top jobs as icon+label, OR a bottom-summoned nav sheet. Kill the hover-to-expand model entirely (no hover on touch). Drop the floating rounded-rail aesthetic for an edge-to-edge bottom bar.

elements.rationale: iOS HIG + UX-Heuristics: primary nav belongs in thumb reach at the bottom; a left drawer behind a top-left hamburger is the least reachable corner on a 390-wide phone. JTBD: nav is the shell's core job, so it must be one tap, always present.

spec.crossCuttingNotes: Patterns here recur across every dashboard surface: (1) A persistent bottom tab bar + a 'More' sheet is the single nav chassis all pages inherit — every content surface must reserve bottom safe-area padding so the bar never overlaps content or the IdleRefreshToast/BugReportTrigger. (2) The Now-tray bottom sheet, its card hierarchy, badge tone split (active orange / late muted), and reduced-motion pulse fallback are reusable anywhere a time-bound prompt appears. (3) Floating-popover-to-bottom-sheet conversion (Refer, Now, Profile) is a shared transform — build one Sheet primitive with grab handle, safe-area padding, and scrim-dismiss (except the forcing overlay). (4) Hover-only affordances must die on touch everywhere: data-tooltip rail tooltips, the reward/Clock chip's hover title in both takeovers, and the BugReportIconButton custom tooltip all need always-visible labels. (5) Bottom-pinned full-width primary CTA is the standard for both takeover flows and the forcing overlay — same ~50px orange button, secondary as outline/text. (6) The orange #f57f20 ceiling and never-color-alone rules hold across all badges/CTAs; the takeovers' navy gradient backdrop is intentionally dark (TIER_POP family) and is NOT the light-theme rule — leave it dark.
openDecisions: Bottom tab bar vs. keep the existing ≤1024 left drawer: adopt a native bottom tab bar (recommended) or retain the current left-slide drawer + hamburger for v1 to minimize churn? This is the biggest fork and dictates every other shell decision.
If bottom tabs: which 3-4 get tab slots? Recommended Dashboard / Menu / Plan / Now — but does Now deserve a tab over Plan, or should Now be a badge on a corner FAB instead, freeing a tab for Account?
Should the cream orange-bordered content-border card be kept on mobile (with tighter padding) or dropped for edge-closer flat content? Affects the visual identity of every page.
Where does Account/Profile live: its own avatar tab or the identity header of the 'More' sheet? And does Report-a-bug stay in profile or move under Help & Support?
Forcing overlay on 360px screens: keep the 72px Sparkles medallion (risking a scroll to reach the CTA) or shrink/drop it to guarantee a no-scroll first glance with the CTA visible?
RevealScreen StatBlock density: force 2-across compact numeric stats (recommended, respects the vertical-cost principle) or allow 1-up stacking for a more dramatic reveal scroll?
Takeover MealGrid columns at 360-390px: 2-across (denser, recommended via the xs/420 intent) vs single-column large cards (more tappable but much taller scroll)?
